editorial.headline: New Motorcycle Retail: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: New-motorcycle retail is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent risk-class moratorium blocks PMA registration for the activity.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47831 defines the retail sale of new motorcycles, expressly including motorised bicycles and mopeds. The point is not merely the word “motorcycle”: the record brings the moped within the same activity boundary. That gives the code a crisp commercial centre—retail trade in new two-wheeled vehicles—and the reading should stay within that stated scope. Its subject is the sale of new motorcycles and the expressly included forms of motorised bicycle and moped.

For registration purposes, this activity is open at every scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That is a full spread across the listed business sizes, rather than an activity confined in the record to one end of the scale spectrum. A founder considering this activity should therefore distinguish scale availability from the separate question of foreign investment. The scale field identifies the business sizes open to the activity; it does not displace either the national PMA position or Bali’s own PMA result.

The national rulebook takes a plain view of foreign investment in this activity. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. Put plainly, the national record allows the foreign stake to reach full ownership for this activity. That national conclusion is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It is the proper national baseline for a foreign-owned business, but it is not the final answer for a registration proposed in Bali.

Bali supplies the hard boundary. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is recorded as Low/Medium-Low across every scope. Under Bali’s stated permanent, island-wide moratorium, all Low and Medium-Low risk activities are blocked for PMA. The record identifies this activity as blocked by that Bali moratorium from May 13, 2026, with Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP as its source. Accordingly, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The island result is not a lower Bali foreign-ownership percentage: it is a block on PMA registration under Bali’s risk-class rule. Nationally the ceiling remains 100%; in Bali the PMA route is unavailable.
